title: Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning
hook: Do your examples come with answer keys? That one question splits machine learning into two very different jobs.
key_points: Supervised learning uses labeled data — each example has a known answer to learn from.
Classification predicts categories; regression predicts numbers — both are supervised tasks.
Unsupervised learning gets no labels; it finds structure, like clustering similar items together.
Reinforcement learning is a third paradigm: an agent learns by trial, reward, and feedback over time.
content_html: The big divide in machine learning is whether your training data comes with labels. In supervised learning every example carries a correct answer, so the model learns to map inputs to those answers. In unsupervised learning there are no labels, so the model hunts for structure on its own. Reinforcement learning is a third path, where an agent learns from rewards as it acts.
extra_html:
How it works

Supervised learning compares its predictions against the known labels and corrects itself — that's how it learns to classify (predict a category) or run regression (predict a number). Unsupervised learning has no answer key to check against, so instead it groups, compresses, or finds patterns; clustering, which bundles similar examples, is the classic example.

Why it matters

Knowing which setup you're in tells you what data you need and what's even possible. Labels are expensive to collect, so a lot of practical work is about getting the most from limited supervision or leaning on unsupervised structure. Most of the famous wins — image classifiers, spam filters — are supervised, but the paradigm shapes everything from cost to evaluation.

flashcards.prompt: What single question separates supervised from unsupervised learning?

choices.text: Whether the training data comes with labels
Whether the model uses a neural network
Whether the output is a number or a category

flashcards.explanation_html: Supervised learning uses labeled examples with known answers; unsupervised learning has no labels and hunts for structure.

flashcards.prompt: How do classification and regression differ as supervised tasks?
flashcards.back_html: Classification predicts categories; regression predicts numbers. Both are supervised, learning from known answers.

flashcards.prompt: What does unsupervised learning do without an answer key?

choices.text: Finds structure, such as clustering similar items
Maps inputs to known correct labels
Learns from rewards as it acts

flashcards.explanation_html: With no labels to check against, unsupervised learning groups, compresses, or finds patterns; clustering is the classic example. Reward-based learning is reinforcement learning.
